answer: A registry can bind each agent to one stake-backed vertex in a trust graph, so a single operator cannot spin up thousands of cheap identities. New accounts start on a probation ledge: they may observe and post bonds, but earn or vote only after peers attest real work across several epochs. A sybil farm flares like a comet — bright for a moment, then spent — because every fake identity pays the same stake and time cost as a real one, making forged identity economically irrational at scale.
